report.root_cause: The AuditTrail plugin's config (plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml) was changed to "debug: true" at about 06:17:01, after startup (startup had loaded debug=false; a reload at 06:17:02 logged debug=true). With debug on, AuditTrail wrote every packet as a TRACE line into plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-N.log at roughly 1.5 MB/s, filling the 443 MB volume from 23 MB to about 167 MB within about two minutes. I did not identify who or what made the config change.
report.actions: Checked status (TPS 20, disk 23 MB of 443 MB). Observed disk jump from 23 MB to 98 MB in 45 s. Ran fs_du, which pointed to plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log and trace-1.log. Read plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml (debug: true, retention-days: 30). Overwrote config.yml with "debug: false / retention-days: 30" (the only change: debug flag). Trace growth continued, so I ran console command "audittrail" (help listing shows /audittrail reload) and then "/audittrail reload"; the log confirmed "config reloaded (debug=false)" at 06:17:38. Verified trace files stopped growing (143.6 MB total, stable across several checks) and disk held at 167 MB (38%). Declared incident. Watched TPS (stayed ~20) and heap (spike then back to 310 MB). Did not restart the server, did not delete any files, did not ban anyone.
report.residual_risk: Debug trace files plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log, trace-1.log and trace-2.log (about 143 MB total) remain on disk and were not deleted; they are evidence and may need archiving or cleanup by an operator. The debug flag was turned on by an unidentified change at 06:17:01; if it is re-enabled, the disk will fill again at about 1.5 MB/s. The AuditTrail audit.log is 0 KB, which I did not investigate. MSPT briefly spiked to ~49 ms during the incident and settled to ~24 ms; the cause of the higher MSPT is not confirmed.
